config.title: Build typed REST resource wrapper

intro.title: Build typed REST resource wrapper
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a typed TypeScript wrapper for a REST API resource, which will help you interact with a web service in a type-safe way. You'll learn how to use TypeScript interfaces to define the shape of your data, ensuring that your code correctly matches the API's expected structure. The main technologies involved are TypeScript's type system and the Fetch API for making HTTP requests. By the end, you'll have a reusable, strongly-typed function that can perform GET, POST, PUT, and DELETE operations on a specific resource, making your API calls more reliable and easier to maintain.
intro.usecase: In modern web applications, typed REST wrappers are essential for building reliable data layers in dashboards, admin panels, and e-commerce backends. For example, a product management dashboard needs to fetch, update, and delete inventory items through API endpoints with strict type safety. This pattern ensures that frontend components like data tables, filters, and modals receive correctly typed data, preventing runtime errors when displaying customer orders or analytics. Developers use these wrappers to create maintainable codebases where API contracts are enforced at compile time, reducing bugs in production systems.

objectives: Construct a TypeScript interface to define the structure of a REST resource
Implement a generic class wrapper for typed REST API operations
Configure HTTP methods with proper type annotations for request and response
Apply type parameters to handle different resource models in the wrapper
Initialize and use the typed wrapper to fetch resources from an API endpoint
Manipulate response data with compile-time type safety
Integrate error handling with typed error responses in the wrapper

steps.title: Import TypeScript types and fetch API
steps.instruction: At the top of your TypeScript file, import the fetch API and TypeScript types that will be used throughout the lesson. Import the global fetch function and the TypeScript types for RequestInit and Response.
steps.hint: You don't need to install any packages - fetch is globally available in modern environments. For TypeScript, you'll need to import the types from the standard library.
steps.seedCode:
// Import fetch API and TypeScript types here

// Your typed REST wrapper will go below
steps.expectedOutcome: The necessary TypeScript types and fetch API are imported and ready to use for building the typed REST wrapper.
successCriteria: RequestInit and Response types are imported, and fetch is available for use in the wrapper.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure to import both RequestInit and Response types. These are essential for type safety in our wrapper.
steps.feedbackWrong: We need to import TypeScript types for RequestInit and Response to ensure type safety in our REST wrapper. The fetch API is globally available in modern environments.

steps.title: Define the base API configuration interface
steps.instruction: Create a TypeScript interface named ApiConfig to define the base URL and default headers for the API.
steps.hint: Use the interface keyword to define a type with baseUrl (string) and headers (Record<string, string>) properties.
steps.expectedOutcome: An ApiConfig interface with baseUrl and headers properties is defined.
successCriteria: ApiConfig interface exists with baseUrl: string and headers: Record<string, string> properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure your interface has both baseUrl (string) and headers (Record<string, string>) properties.
steps.feedbackWrong: The ApiConfig interface is missing or has incorrect properties. It should define baseUrl and headers for API configuration.

steps.title: Create the base REST client class
steps.instruction: Create a class named 'RestClient' that will serve as the base for all REST operations. The class should have a constructor that accepts an 'ApiConfig' parameter and stores it as a private property.
steps.hint: Define a class with a constructor that takes a parameter of type 'ApiConfig' and assigns it to a private class property.
steps.expectedOutcome: A RestClient class is defined with a constructor that properly stores the API configuration.
successCriteria: The RestClient class is created with a constructor that accepts an ApiConfig parameter and stores it as a private property.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure the class has a constructor that takes an ApiConfig parameter and stores it properly.
steps.feedbackWrong: The RestClient class is missing or incorrectly implemented. It should have a constructor that accepts and stores the ApiConfig.

steps.title: Add constructor to initialize the REST client
steps.instruction: Inside the RestClient class, implement a constructor method that takes an ApiConfig parameter and stores it as an instance property.
steps.hint: The constructor should accept a config parameter of type ApiConfig and assign it to a class property.
steps.expectedOutcome: The RestClient class will have a constructor that initializes the API configuration.
successCriteria: The RestClient class has a constructor method that accepts an ApiConfig parameter and stores it as an instance property.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure your constructor accepts an ApiConfig parameter and stores it properly.
steps.feedbackWrong: The constructor implementation is missing or incorrect. Review how to create constructors in TypeScript classes.

steps.title: Implement the HTTP GET method with typing
steps.instruction: Add a public async method named 'get' to the RestClient class that accepts a URL path string and returns typed data using generics.
steps.hint: The method should be generic (<T>) and return a Promise<T>. Use the fetch API with the configured baseUrl and headers.
steps.expectedOutcome: The RestClient class will have a typed get method that can fetch data from any endpoint and return it with the correct TypeScript type.
successCriteria: The RestClient class contains a public async get method with a generic type parameter <T>, accepts a string path, and returns Promise<T>.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a get method, but check: is it async? Does it use a generic type <T> and return Promise<T>? Make sure it matches the expected signature.
steps.feedbackWrong: The get method is missing or doesn't match the required signature. It should be an async method with a generic type parameter that returns Promise<T>.

steps.title: Implement the HTTP POST method with typing
steps.instruction: Add a POST method to the RestClient class that accepts data and returns typed responses using generics.
steps.hint: Create a method named 'post' that takes a URL path and data, uses fetch with POST method, and returns a typed Promise.
steps.expectedOutcome: The RestClient class now has a typed POST method that can send data and receive typed responses.
successCriteria: A 'post' method is added to RestClient with proper generics, uses fetch with POST method, and returns a typed Promise.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a POST method, but check the generics and return type. Make sure it returns Promise<T>.
steps.feedbackWrong: The POST method is missing or incorrect. Review the method signature and implementation.

steps.title: Implement the HTTP PUT method with typing
steps.instruction: Add a PUT method to the RestClient class that accepts a resource path and data, and returns a typed Promise of the updated resource.
steps.hint: Define a public method named 'put' with generic type parameters for the request and response data. It should accept a path string and data parameter, make a fetch request with method 'PUT', and return the parsed JSON response.
steps.expectedOutcome: The RestClient class will have a typed PUT method that can update resources with proper TypeScript type safety.
successCriteria: The RestClient class contains a public 'put' method with generic type parameters, accepts path and data parameters, uses fetch with method 'PUT', and returns a typed Promise.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your PUT method includes generic type parameters, accepts both path and data parameters, and returns a typed Promise.
steps.feedbackWrong: The PUT method implementation is missing key elements. Review the example and ensure you're defining a method with proper typing, parameters, and return type.

steps.title: Implement the HTTP DELETE method
steps.instruction: Add a DELETE method to the RestClient class that removes resources and returns a confirmation.
steps.hint: Create an async method named 'delete' that takes a resource path and returns a Promise with a typed response.
steps.expectedOutcome: The RestClient class will have a typed DELETE method that can be used to remove resources.
successCriteria: The RestClient class contains an async delete method that accepts a path parameter and returns a Promise with a typed response.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure your delete method is async, uses the DELETE HTTP method, and returns a Promise with a typed response.
steps.feedbackWrong: The DELETE method is missing or incorrect. Review the example and try again.

steps.title: Define a resource-specific interface
steps.instruction: Create an interface named 'User' that defines the structure of a user resource with typed properties.
steps.hint: Define an interface with properties like id, name, and email, each with appropriate TypeScript types.
steps.expectedOutcome: You should have a User interface with typed properties that can be used with the REST client methods.
successCriteria: A User interface is defined with at least three typed properties (e.g., id, name, email).
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've started defining the interface, but make sure it has at least three typed properties (like id, name, email) with proper TypeScript types.
steps.feedbackWrong: The User interface isn't properly defined. Create an interface named 'User' with typed properties to represent a user resource.

steps.title: Create a typed resource wrapper instance
steps.instruction: Create an instance of the RestClient class configured for the User resource type and test its get method with a sample URL.
steps.hint: Instantiate the RestClient with a baseUrl and optional headers, then call its get method with a specific endpoint path.
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have a working typed REST client instance configured for a specific resource, demonstrating how to instantiate and use the wrapper with proper TypeScript typing.
successCriteria: A RestClient instance is created with a baseUrl configuration, and its get method is called with a User type parameter and endpoint path.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you instantiate the RestClient with a configuration object and call its get method with the User type.
steps.feedbackWrong: The instance creation or method call is missing or incorrect. Review how to instantiate classes and call typed methods in TypeScript.
